title: Derived reduction modulo varpi^n is left adjoint to restriction of scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ and a scheme $Y$. Use the small pro-etale site $\mathcal C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with its small skeleton and module universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $m\geq1$ put $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ and let $(A_{E,m})_Y$ be its constant sheaf of rings. Define $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}=\varprojlim_{m\geq1}(A_{E,m})_Y$, with transition maps induced by the quotient maps and limit projections $\pi_m$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], and put $S=(A_{E,n})_Y$. Write $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ denote their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\operatorname{Res}_n:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be restriction of scalars along the reduction projection $a=\pi_n:R\to S$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Since restriction of scalars leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged and preserves kernels and cokernels [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is exact; hence, applying it termwise defines a triangulated functor $\operatorname{Res}_n:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. Let $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ be the derived tensor product with $(A_{E,n})_Y$ over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, computed with K-flat resolutions [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Res}_n$: there are bijections

$$
 \Hom_{D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})}\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n},M\bigr)
 \cong
 \Hom_{D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)}\bigl(K,\operatorname{Res}_nM\bigr),
$$

natural in $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ and $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, whose unit is the map $K\to\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ induced by $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\to(A_{E,n})_Y$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$, $S=(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $a=\pi_n:R\to S$. Here the finite constant sheaves, their quotient transitions, the sectionwise inverse-limit ring $R$ and the module derived categories are the constructions explicitly defined in the statement; no finite-field datum is needed. All module categories and localizations use the small skeleton and module universe of the site. Apply the ringed-topos module adjunction to the identity morphism of $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ with coefficient map $a$. Its tensor-formula pullback is $G(N)=S\otimes_R N$ and its pushforward is $F(H)=\operatorname{Res}_n H$. Thus $G\dashv F$ on module sheaves. More explicitly, the forward Hom map sends $v$ to $x\mapsto v(1\otimes x)$; its inverse sends $w$ to $s\otimes x\mapsto s\,w(x)$. These formulas are balanced, commute with restriction, and hence induce maps on the sheafified tensor product. Their composites are identities on generators. The underived unit is consequently $\eta_N:x\mapsto 1\otimes x$, the tensor map induced by $a$.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars changes only the scalar action. A sectionwise kernel therefore remains the same kernel with restricted action. A cokernel is the sheafification of the sectionwise abelian-group quotient in either module category; the restricted action is induced by $a$, so the same quotient and its sheafification give the cokernel after restriction. Thus $F$ preserves kernels and cokernels and is exact, without a hypothesis on $a$ or on the characteristic of $Y$.

proof.text: Apply exact-functor derived factorization to $F$ to obtain its triangulated termwise functor $F_D$. Apply the exact-functor derived theorem: every complex computes $RF$ and its comparison $Q_R F(M)\to RF(Q_S M)$ is an isomorphism. Accordingly identify $RF=F_D=\operatorname{Res}_n$ on the unbounded derived categories. Apply derived change of rings to the actual sheaf map $a:R\to S$, not to the discrete constant sheaf $(\mathcal O_E)_Y$. It supplies an everywhere-defined exact left derived functor $LG$; on a K-flat resolution $p:P\to K$ its value is $Q_S(S\otimes_R P)$. This is precisely the tensor functor named in the item, including its canonical comparisons for different K-flat resolutions.

proof.text: Use the general derived-adjoint-functors theorem with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ restriction and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ tensor extension. Step 1 gives the underived adjunction, and step 3 gives existence at every complex of both derived functors. The theorem yields the canonical bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(LG(K),M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(K,RF(M))$, bifunctorial in both derived variables. With the identifications of step 3 these are exactly the asserted bijections. No boundedness, flatness of $S$ over $R$, derived completeness of $K$, or constructibility is used.

Identify the unit, including its compatibility with the chosen resolution. For K-flat $P$, use the canonical comparison $LG(Q_RP)\cong Q_SG(P)$. In the pre-derived adjunction formula take the target complex to be $G(P)$, its denominator $s$ to be the identity, the source denominator $t$ to be the identity of $P$, and $f=\eta_P:P\to F G(P)$. The termwise homotopy adjunction sends $f$ to $\operatorname{id}_{G(P)}$. The right comparison is the exact-functor identification and the left comparison at $P$ is the K-flat isomorphism. Thus $Q_R(\eta_P)$ is the adjunct of the identity of $LG(Q_RP)$. It is the derived unit on $Q_RP$. For a resolution $p:P\to K$, naturality of the canonical bijection gives $\eta_K=RF(LG(Q_Rp))\circ Q_R(\eta_P)\circ(Q_Rp)^{-1}$. Under the model $LG(K)\cong Q_SG(P)$ this is the roof $K\xleftarrow{p}P\xrightarrow{x\mapsto1\otimes x}F(S\otimes_RP)$. Since $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ is induced by $a$, this proves the claimed description of the unit, independently of the resolution by the same naturality.
